items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: And then I heard Coleman Hawkins play “Body and Soul,” and I thought that’s for me, so I got a tenor saxophone.

ctx.x: How did the saxophone become your instrument of choice?

Well I started on a little piano, and then I started on the clarinet when I was ten years old, and I played that for about five years. And then I heard Coleman Hawkins play “Body and Soul,” and I thought that’s for me, so I got a tenor saxophone. And I started rather late for a lot of people, I was 15. You know people start early in that these days. But that’s the way I got into the saxophone.
So 15, and you were born in 1928, right? So the music around the house and off the radio mostly consisted of what?
